headline: Four more exploited flaws are due for federal fixes, and a vCenter zero-day is in use
plain_summary: CISA added four flaws to its exploited list, three due for federal fixes on November 21. Google says a suspected China-linked group has used a VMware vCenter flaw since September, and Cisco Expressway and Apache Roller flaws are reported exploited. NGINX servers using HTTP/2 also need updating because exploit code is public. Anyone running these products should patch now.

items.title: Four flaws added to CISA's exploited list; three due Nov 21
items.why: Synology DSM, Apache Axis and REDCap are due for federal fixes on November 21 and LiteLLM on December 2, with exploitation reported including ransomware on Synology NAS.
items.action: Find Synology DSM, LiteLLM, Apache Axis and REDCap in your environment and apply vendor fixes where they exist. Axis 1.x is end of life with no fix (migrate or apply the July 12, 2026 commit); keep Axis, LiteLLM and REDCap off the open internet until addressed.

items.title: Google: vCenter zero-day CVE-2026-123890 used in espionage
items.why: Google Threat Intelligence Group says a suspected PRC-nexus actor exploited this unauthenticated bypass in VMware vCenter from early September.
items.action: Apply the Broadcom fix (VMSA-2026-0009; e.g. vCenter 8.0 U3m) now; Broadcom lists no workaround. Restrict inbound access and egress from vCenter, and hunt with the GTIG indicators.

items.title: Cisco Expressway flaw exploited after public exploit code
items.why: F6 reports an attack that spread to two cluster nodes, while Cisco's advisory still says it knows of no malicious use.
items.action: If you run clustered Expressway, upgrade to X15.5.20 now (X14 and earlier must move to a fixed release; no workaround) and restrict TCP 4371-4372 to cluster peers.

items.title: NGINX HTTP/2 flaws allow code execution; exploit code public
items.why: CERT-FR says two NGINX flaws let an unauthenticated attacker run code over HTTP/2, and a public proof of concept exists for one.
items.action: Check every NGINX Open Source and NGINX Plus server that serves HTTP/2. Apply the fixed versions from F5 bulletins K000163926 and K000163928 (1.30.7 or 1.31.9), or disable HTTP/2 until patched; that covers only the HTTP/2 flaws. Review exposed servers for signs of compromise.

items.title: Apache says Roller remote code flaw is being exploited
items.why: The XML-RPC deserialization bug in Roller 4.0.0 to 6.1.4 needs no login, and Apache says it is exploited.
items.action: Upgrade Apache Roller to 6.1.6 or later. If you cannot, set enabledForExtensions to false in WEB-INF/web.xml, remove the /roller-services/xmlrpc mapping and restart; switching off XML-RPC in the admin UI is not enough.

items.title: European Commission confirms AI-generated attack on its systems
items.why: A spokesperson confirmed a campaign detected 22 October that took several applications offline; most are restored and no staff-wide data breach has been detected.
items.action: If you work with EU institutions, expect notices from them and treat unexpected messages claiming to be from Commission staff with care.

items.title: NSA reported to have a tech outage; cyber cause ruled out by sources
items.why: NBC News, citing unnamed sources, reports the outage was not cyber-caused; the cause is not stated and the agency has not been quoted.
